elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ..." — covering both expiry and termination, for any reason.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) states assistance is "at Vendor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data" — the 30-day clock is expressly anchored to the expiry/termination event.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return "in a standard, commonly used machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify that deletion to Customer in writing" — "thereafter" sequences deletion after the limb (b) return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger language: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: The "up to six months" assistance period in limb (a) exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days after expiry or termination, which satisfies the export requirement.

reasons: The finding is correctly characterised as missing: Section 10.1 only ends access "after any agreed transition period" without creating any transition obligation, 10.2 covers only Deliverables and refunds, and Section 15 imposes processing restrictions with no return, export, deletion or certification duty, so no usable exit clause existed.

A single new paragraph inserted after 10.2 carries every preferred element in operative language: trigger on expiry or termination for any reason, up to six months of assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of all Customer Data within thirty days of that event in a standard, commonly used machine-readable format, and certified written deletion thereafter.

The insertion is minimal — one paragraph, no edits to 10.1, 10.2, 15.1, 15.2 or 16.5, no duplicated operative terms, and no obligations beyond the checklist (the "at Customer's request" qualifier on assistance and the sequencing of deletion after return track the model language).

Intent is preserved: the refund and Deliverable-delivery mechanics in 10.2, the survival of rights in 10.1, the processing restrictions in Section 15 and the confidentiality return/destroy regime in 16.5 all continue without contradiction; the new clause supplies the previously absent Customer Data return path rather than displacing any existing allocation.

Non-blocking observation only (correctly left un-redlined and flagged in the rationale): Section 16.5's cross-reference to "Sections 11 and 15" is broken — there is no Section 11 — and would ideally point to the new 10.3. This does not defeat the inserted clause, which stands on its own operative terms, but the drafter may wish to raise it separately.
The margin comment accurately describes what changed, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing; tone and prefix conform.
